one_line_contribution: Transfer across tasks a hierarchical prior over two nuisance statistics of reflective prompt search - rho, the base rate at which an LLM-proposed edit is a true improvement, and the distribution of improvement magnitudes - and use it as the starting belief of a spike-and-slab sequential accept/reject test that replaces GEPA's fixed-minibatch candidate evaluation, leaving proposal and Pareto selection untouched.
closest_prior_work: Two literatures jointly cover the two halves of the method. (1) Best-arm-identification / racing for prompt selection: TRIPLE (Shi et al., 2024, 'Efficient Prompt Optimization Through the Lens of Best Arm Identification') already replaces fixed-budget prompt scoring with adaptive sequential allocation under a rollout budget, and irace / Hoeffding races / Successive Halving do the same in the general configuration-search setting. The proposal's own arm (iii), uninformative racing, concedes this half. (2) Prior-guided and transfer Bayesian optimization: piBO (Hvarfner et al., 2022) injects a user/meta prior into the acquisition function, and RGPE-style ranking-weighted transfer surrogates (Feurer et al.) pool source-task statistics into a target-task prior; meta-learned racing and meta-learned early stopping in AutoML transfer exactly 'how noisy and how rewarding is a proposal here' rather than the search space. The proposal's Related Work dismisses meta-BO on the grounds that it 'requires a shared, low-dimensional, parametric search space', but that objection does not apply to the object actually transferred here - a prior over (rho, effect size) is a two-to-three parameter surrogate-free prior, which is precisely the regime where transferring prior beliefs about outcome statistics rather than the domain is standard. The efficient-LLM-evaluation line (tinyBenchmarks, Anchor Points, IRT-based adaptive evaluation) is a third threat: it transfers item- and candidate-level statistics across tasks specifically to cut evaluation cost, which is the same conceptual move. What is left as novel is the framing sentence ('the search space does not transfer, the noise model does') plus its measurement on GEPA-style runs, which is a positioning delta, not a mechanism.
strongest_objection: The proposal is caught in a dilemma its own risk section (1) half-admits, and no arm in the plan escapes it. The transferred object is two scalars and a shape. Either rho and the effect scale are stable across domains - in which case a hand-set constant prior reproduces TAP and the entire source-harvesting apparatus (6 tasks x 300 rollouts x 3 seeds x 400-example probe scoring of every candidate) buys nothing - or they are task-idiosyncratic, in which case the pooled prior is refuted by Experiment 2. The band in which a *pooled hierarchical* prior beats both a fixed sensible prior and cheap online estimation is narrow, and the proposal's own Falsifiable Prediction (c) shrinks it to roughly rollouts 1-60. Worse, the headline number is arithmetically implausible: a prior over a Bernoulli rate is worth some small effective number of pseudo-observations (at most a handful of candidates, given that between-task heterogeneity across only six source tasks will inflate the pooled variance), yet Prediction (b) claims 2-5 test points over cold-start GEPA at 50 rollouts. Almost all of any such gain must come from adaptivity, not transfer - and adaptivity is arm (iii), uninformative racing, which the proposal itself flags as 'the baseline most likely to erase the contribution'. That leaves the transfer-specific claim as the 1-3 point margin over uninformative racing in Prediction (b), a margin that is very likely inside the treatment-free null-replicate floor that Experiment 1 is designed to establish (the track brief reports that a null replicate reproduced the apparent gain of the best real treatment). Under the proposal's own stated decision rule - 'any effect below the treatment-free null-replicate floor is reported as null regardless of p-value' - the central claim of the paper is then reported as null by construction. Three secondary defects compound this. (a) The power claim is pseudoreplicated: 6 targets x 5 seeds is treated as n=30 paired observations detecting 1.5 points at 80% power, but the unit of generalization for a domain-transfer claim is the task, so the effective n is 6 and the mixed model's task random effect will not rescue a 1-3 point cross-domain claim. Symmetrically, the ICC and leave-one-task-out predictive likelihood in Experiment 2 - billed as the measurement that 'decides the hypothesis independent of downstream gains' - estimate a between-group variance component from six groups, which yields an interval covering nearly the whole [0,1] range and cannot decide anything. (b) The 'strictly paired design' in which the reflection proposal stream is 'replayed identically across evaluation-policy conditions' is impossible past the first divergent accept/reject decision: TAP and cold-start GEPA then hold different Pareto pools, so different parents, so different reflections. The hedge 'where possible' is doing load-bearing work for a variance-reduction claim that expires after roughly one candidate. (c) rho is defined as P(delta>0) with no minimum meaningful delta, estimated against 400-example probe deltas. Near delta=0, where most reflective edits actually live, the sign is dominated by probe noise, so measured rho is biased toward 0.5 and its cross-task stability is partly an artifact of that shrinkage - i.e., the paper could 'confirm' low ICC for measurement reasons. Finally, rho is strongly non-stationary *within* a run (later candidates face a stronger parent, so improvement rates decay); a static per-task scalar ignores the largest variance component, and an online estimator tracks it while the transferred prior cannot, which independently predicts arm (iv) wins.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes would make this reviewable as a main-track contribution. (1) Add the two omitted baselines below and pre-commit that if a hand-set constant prior matches TAP, the paper reports 'no transfer occurred'. (2) Make the transferred object non-trivial: condition rho and the effect-size slab on iteration index and parent validation score (and, ideally, on a cheap task-similarity feature so that transfer can be *predicted* before it is paid for, which is the open question the track brief actually poses). A prior over a decay curve is something an online estimator with 15 candidates genuinely cannot recover; a prior over a single scalar is not. (3) Fix the statistics: state the minimum meaningful delta in the definition of rho and deconvolve probe-set noise from the estimated effect-size distribution; power the between-task variance claim with roughly 20+ source clusters rather than 6, and report ICC with a confidence interval; drop the identical-replay claim or restrict pairing to the pre-divergence prefix; and do the primary power calculation at the task level (n=6), reporting the honest MDE, which will likely show that the 1-3 point transfer-vs-racing gap is not detectable as designed. (4) Derive, before running anything, the effective sample size of the transferred prior in candidate-evaluations, and pre-register the maximum gain that quantity can support; if that ceiling is below the null-replicate floor, the experiment should not be run as the headline claim and should instead be framed as the measurement paper that Experiment 2 already is. Also: actually perform a recent-preprint search and populate the empty collision check.
missing_baseline: Two, both cheap and both potentially fatal. (1) A hand-set constant prior - the same sequential spike-and-slab test with rho and the slab fixed a priori to plausible values (say rho = 0.2-0.3 with a moderate effect scale) and no source harvesting at all. This is the arm that isolates whether anything was *transferred* as opposed to merely *assumed*; the plan's flat-prior racing arm (iii) does not cover it, because a flat prior is not the same as a sensible fixed prior, and the proposal's own Risk Factor (1) concedes the contribution collapses if this arm ties. (2) Cold-start GEPA with a swept minibatch size at matched rollouts. GEPA's fixed minibatch is a hyperparameter, and mechanism (5b), 'more candidates proposed per budget', is obtainable simply by shrinking it from 5 to 2. No reviewer will credit a Bayesian sequential test over a fixed-minibatch baseline whose single relevant hyperparameter was left at its default. A third, weaker omission: no arm reports the reflection-call cost separately, so the token-axis comparison will conflate executor rollouts with frontier reflector spend, and TAP's extra candidates per budget consume more reflector calls than cold-start at the same rollout count.
preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and Related Work opens with '(All citations unverified; literature search was unavailable.)'. By the standard applied here this is a weakness, not a neutral: the proposal's central novelty claim is a negative one - 'a conceptual dissociation none of these make' - and a negative claim over a literature nobody searched is unsupported. This is also the worst possible area in which to skip the search. Adaptive/budget-aware evaluation for GEPA- and MIPRO-style optimizers is exactly the kind of incremental efficiency result that appears on arXiv monthly, and GEPA itself is a 2025 preprint whose follow-ups (adaptive minibatching, early-stopping candidate evaluation, bandit-based candidate selection, budget-aware Pareto maintenance) are the most likely scoop. Named candidates the authors must clear before claiming novelty, from memory and therefore themselves unverified: TRIPLE (Shi et al., 2024) for best-arm-identification prompt selection under a fixed budget; piBO (Hvarfner et al., 2022) and RGPE-style transfer surrogates for injecting meta-learned priors into sequential search; irace and Successive Halving for racing with priors; tinyBenchmarks / Anchor Points / IRT-based adaptive LLM evaluation (2024) for transferring evaluation statistics across tasks to cut scoring cost. If any 2025-2026 preprint has already put an informative, cross-task prior into GEPA's minibatch decision - a very natural thing to try - this proposal's mechanism is gone and only the ICC measurement survives. As submitted, novelty is asserted, not established.
